business_model.claim: Simon sells space in, and services around, retail and mixed-use destinations it owns, develops and manages. The portfolio is mostly malls, Premium Outlets and The Mills. The latest 10-Q lists an interest in 212 U.S. properties (107 malls, 67 Premium Outlets, 16 Mills, six lifestyle centers, 16 other retail) in 38 states and Puerto Rico, plus 42 international properties.
quotes: We own, develop and manage premier shopping, dining, entertainment and mixed-use destinations, which consist primarily of malls, Premium Outlets®, and The Mills®.

business_model.basis: Tenant types are stated in the 10-Q. The lease-income and total-revenue figures come from the income statement.
business_model.claim: The customers are retail, dining, entertainment and other tenants, and lease income is by far the largest revenue line. For the nine months, lease income was 4,969,633 (table in thousands) of total revenue of 5,362,247 (table in thousands).
quotes: We generate the majority of our lease income from retail, dining, entertainment, and other tenants including consideration received from:

business_model.claim: Lease income has a fixed layer and a variable layer. The fixed layer is minimum rent plus fixed common area maintenance (CAM) reimbursements. The variable layer is mainly based on tenants' reported sales, plus reimbursements for real estate taxes, utilities, marketing and other items.
quotes: fixed minimum lease consideration and fixed common area maintenance (CAM) reimbursements, and
variable lease consideration primarily based on tenants’ reported sales, as well as reimbursements for real estate taxes, utilities, marketing and certain other items.

business_model.basis: The fee basis is stated in the 10-Q. The amount is from the income statement line that combines management fees and other revenues.

quotes: Revenues of our management company, after intercompany eliminations, consist primarily of management fees that are typically based upon the revenues of the property being managed.

business_model.basis: Statistics and NOI change are stated in the 10-Q. The CEO view is stated in the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Occupancy and rent per square foot are the main operating levers. In the 10-Q, U.S. Malls and Premium Outlets ending occupancy was 96.5% versus 96.4% a year earlier, and average base minimum rent was $62.75 per square foot versus $59.14, up 6.1%. Management says portfolio NOI rose 7.2% for the nine months, and its CEO cites rising rents, occupancy and shopper traffic.
quotes: Portfolio NOI increased 7.2% for the nine month period in 2026 over the prior year period primarily as a result of improved operations in our domestic and international portfolios and our acquisition activity.
Leasing momentum continued, rents and occupancy increased and shopper traffic growth accelerated for the third consecutive quarter, driving robust retailer sales growth across our portfolio.

Operating cash flow must keep covering distributions, capital expenditures and any buybacks without leaning further on borrowing, since cash and equivalents fell to 569,941 (table in thousands) from 823,147 (table in thousands) at year-end.

growth_thesis.basis: Rates and the ratings strategy are stated in P4; the offsetting effect on earnings is inferred from the interest expense lines in F2.
growth_thesis.claim: Continued access to debt at an acceptable cost is a condition for growth: the effective borrowing rate on consolidated debt rose to 4.07% from 3.74% and interest expense was 844,417 (table in thousands) against 702,509 (table in thousands) in the nine months. Simon must preserve its investment grade ratings and market access to refinance maturities and fund acquisitions without interest cost absorbing the operating gains.
quotes: Our effective overall borrowing rate at September 30, 2026 on our consolidated indebtedness increased 33 basis points to 4.07% as compared to 3.74% at September 30, 2025.
manage our overall financial structure in a fashion that preserves our investment grade credit ratings.
